text:
mina: Brainstorm: what if autoswitch had an adaptive cooldown that lengthens or shortens based on recent signal volatility? The goal is fewer oscillations for noisy workloads but quick reaction for persistent failures. Thoughts?
dave: Nice. So cooldown isn't fixed; it grows if we see repeated short spikes and shrinks when traffic is stable. How do you measure volatility?
linda: Could use rolling variance on error_ratio or a simple burstiness score (count of spikes in last N minutes). Keep it lightweight for realtime.
mina: Prototype policy shape idea:
```
autoswitch:
  adaptive_cooldown:
    enabled: true
    base_ms: 10000
    max_ms: 120000
    volatility_window_ms: 300000
    spike_decay: 0.6  # how quickly spikes reduce the multiplier
```
ops-bot: [alert] 4389998877 - policy p-810 evaluated ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN candidate (current cooldown 10s -> proposed 30s) :information_source:
dave: UX: show the cooldown as a dynamic value in the operator inbox with a small graph of the volatility metric and a slider to pin the cooldown to a fixed value. Also show "suggested" vs "active".
linda: Audit: we must record why cooldown changed: emit ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_ADJUST with fields (policy_id, old_ms, new_ms, reason, volatility_score). That way playback explains the decision path.
telemetry-bot: Proposed events: ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_START, ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_ADJUST, ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_END, ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_OVERRIDE. Metrics: adaptive_cooldown_ms, cooldown_adjust_count, cooldown_volatility_score_histogram.
dave: API for admin changes (SDK):
```
PATCH /v1/policies/{id}
{ "autoswitch": { "adaptive_cooldown": { "base_ms": 10000, "max_ms": 120000 } } }
```
mina: Server-side guard: max_ms <= 10m by default; require tenant opt-in for higher. Also ensure min base_ms >= 1s.
linda: UI affordance: when an operator pins a cooldown, record a ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_OVERRIDE event with user and reason. And in timeline mark pinned state so playback doesn't assume auto adjustments caused the change.
dave: Cost/impact: show an estimated cost delta in the console when cooldown increases (e.g., estimated extra model-seconds) so product can decide good defaults per tier. For dedicated/private defaults differ.
mina: Behavior on trigger: 1) compute volatility_score; 2) scale cooldown = base_ms * (1 + f(volatility)); 3) enter cooldown and emit ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_START. While in cooldown we still sample health; if sustained failure we fallback early (override cooldown) but emit ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_FORCED_FALLBACK with evidence.
telemetry-bot: Suggest payloads for ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_ADJUST: policy_id, prev_ms, new_ms, volatility_score, timestamp, window_stats (error_mean,error_var,p95). Keep window_stats as CSV string to satisfy flat fields.
dave: Tests: simulate workloads with high-frequency tiny spikes vs single long spike. Measure oscillation_count, mean time-to-fallback, and false-fallback rate. Compare adaptive cooldown vs fixed cooldown.
linda: Also test edge: clients that retry aggressively. If cooldown delays fallback, retries could amplify load. Might need an option to signal clients (backoff header) for internal clients.
mina: UX copy: tooltip "Adaptive cooldown: automatically adjusts hold duration based on recent signal volatility to reduce flip-flopping. Operator overrides are logged." Keep short.
dave: I'll mock console panel with volatility sparkline and predicted cooldown timeline. linda: I'll take telemetry ownership and draft event proto and metric names. ops-bot: [note] 4389998905 - scheduled canary run: adaptive-cooldown-sim-3 :gear:
mina: Thanks all. If mocks look good, we can add RFC and a minimal server implementation behind a feature flag. We'll iterate on defaults after canary.
